496	// provisionContext creates a new context from the given configuration and provisions
497	// storage and apps.
498	// If `newCfg` is nil a new empty configuration will be created.
499	// If `replaceAdminServer` is true the local admin server described by the
500	// configuration is provisioned and returned as a pending change: it does not
501	// affect the running admin endpoint until the caller commits it (and must be
502	// rolled back if the new configuration fails).
503	func provisionContext(newCfg *Config, replaceAdminServer bool) (Context, *localAdminChange, error) {
504		// because we will need to roll back any state
505		// modifications if this function errors, we
506		// keep a single error value and scope all
507		// sub-operations to their own functions to
508		// ensure this error value does not get
509		// overridden or missed when it should have
510		// been set by a short assignment
511		var err error
512		var adminChange *localAdminChange
513	
514		if newCfg == nil {
515			newCfg = new(Config)
516		}
517	
518		// create a context within which to load
519		// modules - essentially our new config's
520		// execution environment; be sure that
521		// cleanup occurs when we return if there
522		// was an error; if no error, it will get
523		// cleaned up on next config cycle
524		ctx, cancelCause := NewContextWithCause(Context{Context: context.Background(), cfg: newCfg})
525		defer func() {
526			if err != nil {
527				globalMetrics.configSuccess.Set(0)
528				// if there were any errors during startup,
529				// we should cancel the new context we created
530				// since the associated config won't be used;
531				// this will cause all modules that were newly
532				// provisioned to clean themselves up
533				cancelCause(fmt.Errorf("configuration error: %w", err))
534	
535				// also undo any other state changes we made
536				if currentCtx.cfg != nil {
537					certmagic.Default.Storage = currentCtx.cfg.storage
538				}
539			}
540		}()
541		newCfg.cancelFunc = cancelCause // clean up later
542	
543		// set up logging before anything bad happens
544		if newCfg.Logging == nil {
545			newCfg.Logging = new(Logging)
546		}
547		err = newCfg.Logging.openLogs(ctx)
548		if err != nil {
549			return ctx, nil, err
550		}
551	
552		// create the new filesystem map
553		newCfg.fileSystems = &filesystems.FileSystemMap{}
554	
555		// prepare the new config for use
556		newCfg.apps = make(map[string]App)
557		newCfg.failedApps = make(map[string]error)
558	
559		// set up global storage and make it CertMagic's default storage, too
560		err = func() error {
561			if newCfg.StorageRaw != nil {
562				val, err := ctx.LoadModule(newCfg, "StorageRaw")
563				if err != nil {
564					return fmt.Errorf("loading storage module: %v", err)
565				}
566				stor, err := val.(StorageConverter).CertMagicStorage()
567				if err != nil {
568					return fmt.Errorf("creating storage value: %v", err)
569				}
570				newCfg.storage = stor
571			}
572	
573			if newCfg.storage == nil {
574				newCfg.storage = DefaultStorage
575			}
576			certmagic.Default.Storage = newCfg.storage
577	
578			return nil
579		}()
580		if err != nil {
581			return ctx, nil, err
582		}
583	
584		// provision the admin endpoint for the new configuration, but do
585		// not publish it yet: it is only committed after every app starts
586		// successfully, so a failing configuration cannot take over - or
587		// take down - the endpoint that is still serving the last good one
588		if replaceAdminServer {
589			adminChange, err = prepareLocalAdminServer(newCfg, ctx)
590			if err != nil {
591				return ctx, nil, fmt.Errorf("starting caddy administration endpoint: %v", err)
592			}
593		}
594	
595		// Load and Provision each app and their submodules
596		err = func() error {
597			for appName := range newCfg.AppsRaw {
598				if _, err := ctx.App(appName); err != nil {
599					return err
600				}
601			}
602			return nil
603		}()
604		return ctx, adminChange, err
605	}

607	// ProvisionContext creates a new context from the configuration and provisions storage
608	// and app modules.
609	// The function is intended for testing and advanced use cases only, typically `Run` should be
610	// use to ensure a fully functional caddy instance.
611	// EXPERIMENTAL: While this is public the interface and implementation details of this function may change.
612	func ProvisionContext(newCfg *Config) (Context, error) {
613		ctx, _, err := provisionContext(newCfg, false)
614		return ctx, err
615	}

617	// finishSettingUp should be run after all apps have successfully started.
618	func finishSettingUp(ctx Context, cfg *Config) error {
619		// establish this server's identity (only after apps are loaded
620		// so that cert management of this endpoint doesn't prevent user's
621		// servers from starting which likely also use HTTP/HTTPS ports;
622		// but before remote management which may depend on these creds)
623		err := manageIdentity(ctx, cfg)
624		if err != nil {
625			return fmt.Errorf("provisioning remote admin endpoint: %v", err)
626		}
627	
628		// replace any remote admin endpoint
629		err = replaceRemoteAdminServer(ctx, cfg)
630		if err != nil {
631			return fmt.Errorf("provisioning remote admin endpoint: %v", err)
632		}
633	
634		// if dynamic config is requested, set that up and run it
635		if cfg != nil && cfg.Admin != nil && cfg.Admin.Config != nil && cfg.Admin.Config.LoadRaw != nil {
636			val, err := ctx.LoadModule(cfg.Admin.Config, "LoadRaw")
637			if err != nil {
638				return fmt.Errorf("loading config loader module: %s", err)
639			}
640	
641			logger := Log().Named("config_loader").With(
642				zap.String("module", val.(Module).CaddyModule().ID.Name()),
643				zap.Int("load_delay", int(cfg.Admin.Config.LoadDelay)))
644	
645			runLoadedConfig := func(config []byte) error {
646				logger.Info("applying dynamically-loaded config")
647				err := changeConfig(http.MethodPost, "/"+rawConfigKey, config, "", false)
648				if errors.Is(err, errSameConfig) {
649					return err
650				}
651				if err != nil {
652					logger.Error("failed to run dynamically-loaded config", zap.Error(err))
653					return err
654				}
655				logger.Info("successfully applied dynamically-loaded config")
656				return nil
657			}
658	
659			if cfg.Admin.Config.LoadDelay > 0 {
660				go func() {
661					// the loop is here to iterate ONLY if there is an error, a no-op config load,
662					// or an unchanged config; in which case we simply wait the delay and try again
663					for {
664						timer := time.NewTimer(time.Duration(cfg.Admin.Config.LoadDelay))
665						select {
666						case <-timer.C:
667							loadedConfig, err := val.(ConfigLoader).LoadConfig(ctx)
668							if err != nil {
669								logger.Error("failed loading dynamic config; will retry", zap.Error(err))
670								continue
671							}
672							if loadedConfig == nil {
673								logger.Info("dynamically-loaded config was nil; will retry")
674								continue
675							}
676							err = runLoadedConfig(loadedConfig)
677							if errors.Is(err, errSameConfig) {
678								logger.Info("dynamically-loaded config was unchanged; will retry")
679								continue
680							}
681						case <-ctx.Done():
682							if !timer.Stop() {
683								<-timer.C
684							}
685							logger.Info("stopping dynamic config loading")
686						}
687						break
688					}
689				}()
690			} else {
691				// if no LoadDelay is provided, will load config synchronously
692				loadedConfig, err := val.(ConfigLoader).LoadConfig(ctx)
693				if err != nil {
694					return fmt.Errorf("loading dynamic config from %T: %v", val, err)
695				}
696				// do this in a goroutine so current config can finish being loaded; otherwise deadlock
697				go func() { _ = runLoadedConfig(loadedConfig) }()
698			}
699		}
700	
701		return nil
702	}
703	
704	// ConfigLoader is a type that can load a Caddy config. If
705	// the return value is non-nil, it must be valid Caddy JSON;
706	// if nil or with non-nil error, it is considered to be a
707	// no-op load and may be retried later.
708	type ConfigLoader interface {
709		LoadConfig(Context) ([]byte, error)
710	}

712	// Stop stops running the current configuration.
713	// It is the antithesis of Run(). This function
714	// will log any errors that occur during the
715	// stopping of individual apps and continue to
716	// stop the others. Stop should only be called
717	// if not replacing with a new config.
718	func Stop() error {
719		currentCtxMu.RLock()
720		ctx := currentCtx
721		currentCtxMu.RUnlock()
722	
723		rawCfgMu.Lock()
724		unsyncedStop(ctx)
725	
726		currentCtxMu.Lock()
727		currentCtx = Context{}
728		currentCtxMu.Unlock()
729	
730		rawCfgJSON = nil
731		rawCfgIndex = nil
732		rawCfg[rawConfigKey] = nil
733		rawCfgMu.Unlock()
734	
735		return nil
736	}
737	
738	// unsyncedStop stops ctx from running, but has
739	// no locking around ctx. It is a no-op if ctx has a
740	// nil cfg. If any app returns an error when stopping,
741	// it is logged and the function continues stopping
742	// the next app. This function assumes all apps in
743	// ctx were successfully started first.
744	//
745	// A lock on rawCfgMu is required, even though this
746	// function does not access rawCfg, that lock
747	// synchronizes the stop/start of apps.
748	func unsyncedStop(ctx Context) {
749		if ctx.cfg == nil {
750			return
751		}
752	
753		// TODO: This event is experimental and subject to change.
754		ctx.emitEvent("stopping", nil)
755	
756		// stop each app
757		for name, a := range ctx.cfg.apps {
758			err := a.Stop()
759			if err != nil {
760				log.Printf("[ERROR] stop %s: %v", name, err)
761			}
762		}
763	
764		// clean up all modules
765		ctx.cfg.cancelFunc(fmt.Errorf("stopping apps"))
766	}

768	// Validate loads, provisions, and validates
769	// cfg, but does not start running it.
770	func Validate(cfg *Config) error {
771		_, err := run(cfg, false)
772		if err == nil {
773			cfg.cancelFunc(fmt.Errorf("validation complete")) // call Cleanup on all modules
774		}
775		return err
776	}

778	// exitProcess exits the process as gracefully as possible,
779	// but it always exits, even if there are errors doing so.
780	// It stops all apps, cleans up external locks, removes any
781	// PID file, and shuts down admin endpoint(s) in a goroutine.
782	// Errors are logged along the way, and an appropriate exit
783	// code is emitted.
784	func exitProcess(ctx context.Context, logger *zap.Logger) {
785		// let the rest of the program know we're quitting; only do it once
786		if !exiting.CompareAndSwap(false, true) {
787			return
788		}
789	
790		// give the OS or service/process manager our 2 weeks' notice: we quit
791		if err := notify.Stopping(); err != nil {
792			Log().Error("unable to notify service manager of stopping state", zap.Error(err))
793		}
794	
795		if logger == nil {
796			logger = Log()
797		}
798		logger.Warn("exiting; byeee!! 👋")
799	
800		exitCode := ExitCodeSuccess
801		lastContext := ActiveContext()
802	
803		// stop all apps
804		if err := Stop(); err != nil {
805			logger.Error("failed to stop apps", zap.Error(err))
806			exitCode = ExitCodeFailedQuit
807		}
808	
809		// clean up certmagic locks
810		certmagic.CleanUpOwnLocks(ctx, logger)
811	
812		// remove pidfile
813		if pidfile != "" {
814			err := os.Remove(pidfile)
815			if err != nil {
816				logger.Error("cleaning up PID file:",
817					zap.String("pidfile", pidfile),
818					zap.Error(err))
819				exitCode = ExitCodeFailedQuit
820			}
821		}
822	
823		// execute any process-exit callbacks
824		for _, exitFunc := range lastContext.exitFuncs {
825			exitFunc(ctx)
826		}
827		exitFuncsMu.Lock()
828		for _, exitFunc := range exitFuncs {
829			exitFunc(ctx)
830		}
831		exitFuncsMu.Unlock()
832	
833		// shut down admin endpoint(s) in goroutines so that
834		// if this function was called from an admin handler,
835		// it has a chance to return gracefully
836		// use goroutine so that we can finish responding to API request
837		go func() {
838			defer func() {
839				logger = logger.With(zap.Int("exit_code", exitCode))
840				if exitCode == ExitCodeSuccess {
841					logger.Info("shutdown complete")
842				} else {
843					logger.Error("unclean shutdown")
844				}
845				os.Exit(exitCode)
846			}()
847	
848			if remoteAdminServer != nil {
849				err := stopAdminServer(remoteAdminServer)
850				if err != nil {
851					exitCode = ExitCodeFailedQuit
852					logger.Error("failed to stop remote admin server gracefully", zap.Error(err))
853				}
854			}
855			if localAdminServer != nil {
856				err := stopAdminServer(localAdminServer)
857				if err != nil {
858					exitCode = ExitCodeFailedQuit
859					logger.Error("failed to stop local admin server gracefully", zap.Error(err))
860				}
861			}
862		}()
863	}

865	var exiting atomic.Bool
866	
867	// Exiting returns true if the process is exiting.
868	// EXPERIMENTAL API: subject to change or removal.
869	func Exiting() bool { return exiting.Load() }

871	// OnExit registers a callback to invoke during process exit.
872	// This registration is PROCESS-GLOBAL, meaning that each
873	// function should only be registered once forever, NOT once
874	// per config load (etc).
875	//
876	// EXPERIMENTAL API: subject to change or removal.
877	func OnExit(f func(context.Context)) {
878		exitFuncsMu.Lock()
879		exitFuncs = append(exitFuncs, f)
880		exitFuncsMu.Unlock()
881	}

883	var (
884		exitFuncs   []func(context.Context)
885		exitFuncsMu sync.Mutex
886	)

888	// Duration can be an integer or a string. An integer is
889	// interpreted as nanoseconds. If a string, it is a Go
890	// time.Duration value such as `300ms`, `1.5h`, or `2h45m`;
891	// valid units are `ns`, `us`/`µs`, `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, and `d`.
892	type Duration time.Duration
893	
894	// UnmarshalJSON satisfies json.Unmarshaler.
895	func (d *Duration) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error {
896		if len(b) == 0 {
897			return io.EOF
898		}
899		var dur time.Duration
900		var err error
901		if b[0] == byte('"') && b[len(b)-1] == byte('"') {
902			dur, err = ParseDuration(strings.Trim(string(b), `"`))
903		} else {
904			err = json.Unmarshal(b, &dur)
905		}
906		*d = Duration(dur)
907		return err
908	}
909	
910	// ParseDuration parses a duration string, adding
911	// support for the "d" unit meaning number of days,
912	// where a day is assumed to be 24h. The maximum
913	// input string length is 1024.
914	func ParseDuration(s string) (time.Duration, error) {
915		if len(s) > 1024 {
916			return 0, fmt.Errorf("parsing duration: input string too long")
917		}
918		var inNumber bool
919		var numStart int
920		for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
921			ch := s[i]
922			if ch == 'd' {
923				daysStr := s[numStart:i]
924				days, err := strconv.ParseFloat(daysStr, 64)
925				if err != nil {
926					return 0, err
927				}
928				hours := days * 24.0
929				hoursStr := strconv.FormatFloat(hours, 'f', -1, 64)
930				s = s[:numStart] + hoursStr + "h" + s[i+1:]
931				i--
932				continue
933			}
934			if !inNumber {
935				numStart = i
936			}
937			inNumber = (ch >= '0' && ch <= '9') || ch == '.' || ch == '-' || ch == '+'
938		}
939		return time.ParseDuration(s)
940	}

942	// InstanceID returns the UUID for this instance, and generates one if it
943	// does not already exist. The UUID is stored in the local data directory,
944	// regardless of storage configuration, since each instance is intended to
945	// have its own unique ID.
946	func InstanceID() (uuid.UUID, error) {
947		appDataDir := AppDataDir()
948		uuidFilePath := filepath.Join(appDataDir, "instance.uuid")
949		uuidFileBytes, err := os.ReadFile(uuidFilePath)
950		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
951			uuid, err := uuid.NewRandom()
952			if err != nil {
953				return uuid, err
954			}
955			err = os.MkdirAll(appDataDir, 0o700)
956			if err != nil {
957				return uuid, err
958			}
959			err = os.WriteFile(uuidFilePath, []byte(uuid.String()), 0o600)
960			return uuid, err
961		} else if err != nil {
962			return [16]byte{}, err
963		}
964		return uuid.ParseBytes(uuidFileBytes)
965	}

969	// need to manually set Caddy's version. If no other version
970	// information is available, the short form version (see
971	// Version()) will be set to CustomVersion, and the full version

973	//

975	//
976	//	-ldflags '-X github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2.CustomVersion=v2.6.2'
977	//
978	// for example.

980	
981	// CustomBinaryName is an optional string that overrides the root
982	// command name from the default of "caddy". This is useful for
983	// downstream projects that embed Caddy but use a different binary
984	// name. Shell completions and help text will use this name instead
985	// of "caddy".
986	//
987	// Set this variable during `go build` with `-ldflags`:
988	//
989	//	-ldflags '-X github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2.CustomBinaryName=my_custom_caddy'
990	//
991	// for example.
992	var CustomBinaryName string
993	
994	// CustomLongDescription is an optional string that overrides the
995	// long description of the root Cobra command. This is useful for
996	// downstream projects that embed Caddy but want different help
997	// output.
998	//
999	// Set this variable in an init() function of a package that is
1000	// imported by your main:
1001	//
1002	//	func init() {
1003	//	    caddy.CustomLongDescription = "My custom server based on Caddy..."
1004	//	}
1005	//
1006	// for example.
1007	var CustomLongDescription string
1008	
1009	// Version returns the Caddy version in a simple/short form, and
1010	// a full version string. The short form will not have spaces and
1011	// is intended for User-Agent strings and similar, but may be
1012	// omitting valuable information. Note that Caddy must be compiled
1013	// in a special way to properly embed complete version information.
1014	// First this function tries to get the version from the embedded
1015	// build info provided by go.mod dependencies; then it tries to
1016	// get info from embedded VCS information, which requires having
1017	// built Caddy from a git repository. If no version is available,
1018	// this function returns "(devel)" because Go uses that, but for
1019	// the simple form we change it to "unknown". If still no version
1020	// is available (e.g. no VCS repo), then it will use CustomVersion;
1021	// CustomVersion is always prepended to the full version string.
1022	//
1023	// See relevant Go issues: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/29228
1024	// and https://github.com/golang/go/issues/50603.
1025	//
1026	// This function is experimental and subject to change or removal.
1027	func Version() (simple, full string) {
1028		// the currently-recommended way to build Caddy involves
1029		// building it as a dependency so we can extract version
1030		// information from go.mod tooling; once the upstream
1031		// Go issues are fixed, we should just be able to use
1032		// bi.Main... hopefully.
1033		var module *debug.Module
1034		bi, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo()
1035		if !ok {
1036			if CustomVersion != "" {
1037				full = CustomVersion
1038				simple = CustomVersion
1039				return simple, full
1040			}
1041			full = "unknown"
1042			simple = "unknown"
1043			return simple, full
1044		}
1045		// find the Caddy module in the dependency list
1046		for _, dep := range bi.Deps {
1047			if dep.Path == ImportPath {
1048				module = dep
1049				break
1050			}
1051		}
1052		if module != nil {
1053			simple, full = module.Version, module.Version
1054			if module.Sum != "" {
1055				full += " " + module.Sum
1056			}
1057			if module.Replace != nil {
1058				full += " => " + module.Replace.Path
1059				if module.Replace.Version != "" {
1060					simple = module.Replace.Version + "_custom"
1061					full += "@" + module.Replace.Version
1062				}
1063				if module.Replace.Sum != "" {
1064					full += " " + module.Replace.Sum
1065				}
1066			}
1067		}
1068	
1069		if full == "" {
1070			var vcsRevision string
1071			var vcsTime time.Time
1072			var vcsModified bool
1073			for _, setting := range bi.Settings {
1074				switch setting.Key {
1075				case "vcs.revision":
1076					vcsRevision = setting.Value
1077				case "vcs.time":
1078					vcsTime, _ = time.Parse(time.RFC3339, setting.Value)
1079				case "vcs.modified":
1080					vcsModified, _ = strconv.ParseBool(setting.Value)
1081				}
1082			}
1083	
1084			if vcsRevision != "" {
1085				var modified string
1086				if vcsModified {
1087					modified = "+modified"
1088				}
1089				full = fmt.Sprintf("%s%s (%s)", vcsRevision, modified, vcsTime.Format(time.RFC822))
1090				simple = vcsRevision
1091	
1092				// use short checksum for simple, if hex-only
1093				if _, err := hex.DecodeString(simple); err == nil {
1094					simple = simple[:8]
1095				}
1096	
1097				// append date to simple since it can be convenient
1098				// to know the commit date as part of the version
1099				if !vcsTime.IsZero() {
1100					simple += "-" + vcsTime.Format("20060102")
1101				}
1102			}
1103		}
1104	
1105		if full == "" {
1106			if CustomVersion != "" {
1107				full = CustomVersion
1108			} else {
1109				full = "unknown"
1110			}
1111		} else if CustomVersion != "" {
1112			full = CustomVersion + " " + full
1113		}
1114	
1115		if simple == "" || simple == "(devel)" {
1116			if CustomVersion != "" {
1117				simple = CustomVersion
1118			} else {
1119				simple = "unknown"
1120			}
1121		}
1122	
1123		return simple, full
1124	}
1125	
1126	// Event represents something that has happened or is happening.
1127	// An Event value is not synchronized, so it should be copied if
1128	// being used in goroutines.
1129	//
1130	// EXPERIMENTAL: Events are subject to change.
1131	type Event struct {
1132		// If non-nil, the event has been aborted, meaning
1133		// propagation has stopped to other handlers and
1134		// the code should stop what it was doing. Emitters
1135		// may choose to use this as a signal to adjust their
1136		// code path appropriately.
1137		Aborted error
1138	
1139		// The data associated with the event. Usually the
1140		// original emitter will be the only one to set or
1141		// change these values, but the field is exported
1142		// so handlers can have full access if needed.
1143		// However, this map is not synchronized, so
1144		// handlers must not use this map directly in new
1145		// goroutines; instead, copy the map to use it in a
1146		// goroutine. Data may be nil.
1147		Data map[string]any
1148	
1149		id     uuid.UUID
1150		ts     time.Time
1151		name   string
1152		origin Module
1153	}
1154	
1155	// NewEvent creates a new event, but does not emit the event. To emit an
1156	// event, call Emit() on the current instance of the caddyevents app instead.
1157	//
1158	// EXPERIMENTAL: Subject to change.
1159	func NewEvent(ctx Context, name string, data map[string]any) (Event, error) {
1160		id, err := uuid.NewRandom()
1161		if err != nil {
1162			return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("generating new event ID: %v", err)
1163		}
1164		name = strings.ToLower(name)
1165		return Event{
1166			Data:   data,
1167			id:     id,
1168			ts:     time.Now(),
1169			name:   name,
1170			origin: ctx.Module(),
1171		}, nil
1172	}
1173	
1174	func (e Event) ID() uuid.UUID        { return e.id }
1175	func (e Event) Timestamp() time.Time { return e.ts }
1176	func (e Event) Name() string         { return e.name }
1177	func (e Event) Origin() Module       { return e.origin } // Returns the module that originated the event. May be nil, usually if caddy core emits the event.
1178	
1179	// CloudEvent exports event e as a structure that, when
1180	// serialized as JSON, is compatible with the
1181	// CloudEvents spec.
1182	func (e Event) CloudEvent() CloudEvent {
1183		dataJSON, _ := json.Marshal(e.Data)
1184		var source string
1185		if e.Origin() == nil {
1186			source = "caddy"
1187		} else {
1188			source = string(e.Origin().CaddyModule().ID)
1189		}
1190		return CloudEvent{
1191			ID:              e.id.String(),
1192			Source:          source,
1193			SpecVersion:     "1.0",
1194			Type:            e.name,
1195			Time:            e.ts,
1196			DataContentType: "application/json",
1197			Data:            dataJSON,
1198		}
1199	}
1200	
1201	// CloudEvent is a JSON-serializable structure that
1202	// is compatible with the CloudEvents specification.
1203	// See https://cloudevents.io.
1204	// EXPERIMENTAL: Subject to change.
1205	type CloudEvent struct {
1206		ID              string          `json:"id"`
1207		Source          string          `json:"source"`
1208		SpecVersion     string          `json:"specversion"`
1209		Type            string          `json:"type"`
1210		Time            time.Time       `json:"time"`
1211		DataContentType string          `json:"datacontenttype,omitempty"`
1212		Data            json.RawMessage `json:"data,omitempty"`
1213	}

1215	// ErrEventAborted cancels an event.
1216	var ErrEventAborted = errors.New("event aborted")

1218	// ActiveContext returns the currently-active context.
1219	// This function is experimental and might be changed
1220	// or removed in the future.
1221	func ActiveContext() Context {
1222		currentCtxMu.RLock()
1223		defer currentCtxMu.RUnlock()
1224		return currentCtx
1225	}
1226	
1227	// CtxKey is a value type for use with context.WithValue.
1228	type CtxKey string
1229	
1230	// This group of variables pertains to the current configuration.
1231	var (
1232		// currentCtx is the root context for the currently-running
1233		// configuration, which can be accessed through this value.
1234		// If the Config contained in this value is not nil, then
1235		// a config is currently active/running.
1236		currentCtx   Context
1237		currentCtxMu sync.RWMutex
1238	
1239		// rawCfg is the current, generic-decoded configuration;
1240		// we initialize it as a map with one field ("config")
1241		// to maintain parity with the API endpoint and to avoid
1242		// the special case of having to access/mutate the variable
1243		// directly without traversing into it.
1244		rawCfg = map[string]any{
1245			rawConfigKey: nil,
1246		}
1247	
1248		// rawCfgJSON is the JSON-encoded form of rawCfg. Keeping
1249		// this around avoids an extra Marshal call during changes.
1250		rawCfgJSON []byte
1251	
1252		// rawCfgIndex is the map of user-assigned ID to expanded
1253		// path, for converting /id/ paths to /config/ paths.
1254		rawCfgIndex map[string]string
1255	
1256		// rawCfgMu protects all the rawCfg fields and also
1257		// essentially synchronizes config changes/reloads.
1258		rawCfgMu sync.RWMutex
1259	)
1260	
1261	// lastConfigFile and lastConfigAdapter remember the source config
1262	// file and adapter used when Caddy was started via the CLI "run" command.
1263	// These are consulted by the SIGUSR1 handler to attempt reloading from
1264	// the same source. They are intentionally not set for other entrypoints
1265	// such as "caddy start" or subcommands like file-server.
1266	var (
1267		lastConfigMu      sync.RWMutex
1268		lastConfigFile    string
1269		lastConfigAdapter string
1270	)
1271	
1272	// reloadFromSourceFunc is the type of stored callback
1273	// which is called when we receive a SIGUSR1 signal.
1274	type reloadFromSourceFunc func(file, adapter string) error
1275	
1276	// reloadFromSourceCallback is the stored callback
1277	// which is called when we receive a SIGUSR1 signal.
1278	var reloadFromSourceCallback reloadFromSourceFunc
1279	
1280	// errReloadFromSourceUnavailable is returned when no reload-from-source callback is set.
1281	var errReloadFromSourceUnavailable = errors.New("reload from source unavailable in this process") //nolint:unused
1282	
1283	// SetLastConfig records the given source file and adapter as the
1284	// last-known external configuration source. Intended to be called
1285	// only when starting via "caddy run --config <file> --adapter <adapter>".
1286	func SetLastConfig(file, adapter string, fn reloadFromSourceFunc) {
1287		lastConfigMu.Lock()
1288		lastConfigFile = file
1289		lastConfigAdapter = adapter
1290		reloadFromSourceCallback = fn
1291		lastConfigMu.Unlock()
1292	}
1293	
1294	// ClearLastConfigIfDifferent clears the recorded last-config if the provided
1295	// source file/adapter do not match the recorded last-config. If both srcFile
1296	// and srcAdapter are empty, the last-config is cleared.
1297	func ClearLastConfigIfDifferent(srcFile, srcAdapter string) {
1298		if (srcFile != "" || srcAdapter != "") && lastConfigMatches(srcFile, srcAdapter) {
1299			return
1300		}
1301		SetLastConfig("", "", nil)
1302	}
1303	
1304	// getLastConfig returns the last-known config file and adapter.
1305	func getLastConfig() (file, adapter string, fn reloadFromSourceFunc) {
1306		lastConfigMu.RLock()
1307		f, a, cb := lastConfigFile, lastConfigAdapter, reloadFromSourceCallback
1308		lastConfigMu.RUnlock()
1309		return f, a, cb
1310	}
1311	
1312	// lastConfigMatches returns true if the provided source file and/or adapter
1313	// matches the recorded last-config. Matching rules (in priority order):
1314	// 1. If srcAdapter is provided and differs from the recorded adapter, no match.
1315	// 2. If srcFile exactly equals the recorded file, match.
1316	// 3. If both sides can be made absolute and equal, match.
1317	// 4. If basenames are equal, match.
1318	func lastConfigMatches(srcFile, srcAdapter string) bool {
1319		lf, la, _ := getLastConfig()
1320	
1321		// If adapter is provided, it must match.
1322		if srcAdapter != "" && srcAdapter != la {
1323			return false
1324		}
1325	
1326		// Quick equality check.
1327		if srcFile == lf {
1328			return true
1329		}
1330	
1331		// Try absolute path comparison.
1332		sAbs, sErr := filepath.Abs(srcFile)
1333		lAbs, lErr := filepath.Abs(lf)
1334		if sErr == nil && lErr == nil && sAbs == lAbs {
1335			return true
1336		}
1337	
1338		// Final fallback: basename equality.
1339		if filepath.Base(srcFile) == filepath.Base(lf) {
1340			return true
1341		}
1342	
1343		return false
1344	}
1345	
1346	// errSameConfig is returned if the new config is the same
1347	// as the old one. This isn't usually an actual, actionable
1348	// error; it's mostly a sentinel value.
1349	var errSameConfig = errors.New("config is unchanged")
1350	
1351	// ImportPath is the package import path for Caddy core.
1352	// This identifier may be removed in the future.
1353	const ImportPath = "github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2"
1354

41	// App is a robust, production-ready HTTP server.
42	//
43	// HTTPS is enabled by default if host matchers with qualifying names are used
44	// in any of routes; certificates are automatically provisioned and renewed.
45	// Additionally, automatic HTTPS will also enable HTTPS for servers that listen
46	// only on the HTTPS port but which do not have any TLS connection policies
47	// defined by adding a good, default TLS connection policy.
48	//
49	// In HTTP routes, additional placeholders are available (replace any `*`):
50	//
51	// Placeholder | Description
52	// ------------|---------------
53	// `{http.request.body}` | The request body (⚠️ inefficient; use only for debugging)
54	// `{http.request.body_base64}` | The request body, base64-encoded (⚠️ for debugging)
55	// `{http.request.cookie.*}` | HTTP request cookie
56	// `{http.request.duration}` | Time up to now spent handling the request (after decoding headers from client)
57	// `{http.request.duration_ms}` | Same as 'duration', but in milliseconds.
58	// `{http.request.uuid}` | The request unique identifier
59	// `{http.request.header.*}` | Specific request header field
60	// `{http.request.host}` | The host part of the request's Host header
61	// `{http.request.host.labels.*}` | Request host labels (0-based from right); e.g. for foo.example.com: 0=com, 1=example, 2=foo
62	// `{http.request.hostport}` | The host and port from the request's Host header
63	// `{http.request.method}` | The request method
64	// `{http.request.orig_method}` | The request's original method
65	// `{http.request.orig_uri}` | The request's original URI
66	// `{http.request.orig_uri.path}` | The request's original path
67	// `{http.request.orig_uri.path.*}` | Parts of the original path, split by `/` (0-based from left)
68	// `{http.request.orig_uri.path.dir}` | The request's original directory
69	// `{http.request.orig_uri.path.file}` | The request's original filename
70	// `{http.request.orig_uri.query}` | The request's original query string (without `?`)
71	// `{http.request.orig_uri.prefixed_query}` | The request's original query string with a `?` prefix, if non-empty
72	// `{http.request.port}` | The port part of the request's Host header
73	// `{http.request.proto}` | The protocol of the request
74	// `{http.request.local.host}` | The host (IP) part of the local address the connection arrived on
75	// `{http.request.local.port}` | The port part of the local address the connection arrived on
76	// `{http.request.local}` | The local address the connection arrived on
77	// `{http.request.remote.host}` | The host (IP) part of the remote client's address, if available (not known with HTTP/3 early data)
78	// `{http.request.remote.port}` | The port part of the remote client's address
79	// `{http.request.remote}` | The address of the remote client

86	// `{http.request.tls.server_name}` | The server name requested by the client, if any
87	// `{http.request.tls.ech}` | Whether ECH was offered by the client and accepted by the server
88	// `{http.request.tls.client.fingerprint}` | The SHA256 checksum of the client certificate

100	// `{http.request.uri}` | The full request URI
101	// `{http.request.uri_escaped}` | The full request URI with query-style URL encoding applied (using url.QueryEscape)
102	// `{http.request.uri.path}` | The path component of the request URI
103	// `{http.request.uri.path_escaped}` | The path component of the request URI with query-style URL encoding applied (using url.QueryEscape)
104	// `{http.request.uri.path.*}` | Parts of the path, split by `/` (0-based from left)
105	// `{http.request.uri.path.dir}` | The directory, excluding leaf filename
106	// `{http.request.uri.path.file}` | The filename of the path, excluding directory
107	// `{http.request.uri.query}` | The query string (without `?`)
108	// `{http.request.uri.query_escaped}` | The query string with query-style URL encoding applied (using url.QueryEscape)
109	// `{http.request.uri.prefixed_query}` | The query string with a `?` prefix, if non-empty
110	// `{http.request.uri.query.*}` | Individual query string value
111	// `{http.response.header.*}` | Specific response header field
112	// `{http.vars.*}` | Custom variables in the HTTP handler chain
113	// `{http.shutting_down}` | True if the HTTP app is shutting down
114	// `{http.time_until_shutdown}` | Time until HTTP server shutdown, if scheduled
115	type App struct {
116		// HTTPPort specifies the port to use for HTTP (as opposed to HTTPS),
117		// which is used when setting up HTTP->HTTPS redirects or ACME HTTP
118		// challenge solvers. Default: 80.
119		HTTPPort int `json:"http_port,omitempty"`
120	
121		// HTTPSPort specifies the port to use for HTTPS, which is used when
122		// solving the ACME TLS-ALPN challenges, or whenever HTTPS is needed
123		// but no specific port number is given. Default: 443.
124		HTTPSPort int `json:"https_port,omitempty"`
125	
126		// GracePeriod is how long to wait for active connections when shutting
127		// down the servers. During the grace period, no new connections are
128		// accepted, idle connections are closed, and active connections will
129		// be given the full length of time to become idle and close.
130		// Once the grace period is over, connections will be forcefully closed.
131		// If zero, the grace period is eternal. Default: 0.
132		GracePeriod caddy.Duration `json:"grace_period,omitempty"`
133	
134		// ShutdownDelay is how long to wait before initiating the grace
135		// period. When this app is stopping (e.g. during a config reload or
136		// process exit), all servers will be shut down. Normally this immediately
137		// initiates the grace period. However, if this delay is configured, servers
138		// will not be shut down until the delay is over. During this time, servers
139		// continue to function normally and allow new connections. At the end, the
140		// grace period will begin. This can be useful to allow downstream load
141		// balancers time to move this instance out of the rotation without hiccups.
142		//
143		// When shutdown has been scheduled, placeholders {http.shutting_down} (bool)
144		// and {http.time_until_shutdown} (duration) may be useful for health checks.
145		ShutdownDelay caddy.Duration `json:"shutdown_delay,omitempty"`
146	
147		// Servers is the list of servers, keyed by arbitrary names chosen
148		// at your discretion for your own convenience; the keys do not
149		// affect functionality.
150		Servers map[string]*Server `json:"servers,omitempty"`
151	
152		// If set, metrics observations will be enabled.
153		// This setting is EXPERIMENTAL and subject to change.
154		Metrics *Metrics `json:"metrics,omitempty"`
155	
156		ctx    caddy.Context
157		logger *zap.Logger
158		tlsApp *caddytls.TLS
159	
160		// stopped indicates whether the app has stopped
161		// It can only happen if it has started successfully in the first place.
162		// Otherwise, Cleanup will call Stop to clean up resources.
163		stopped bool
164	
165		// used temporarily between phases 1 and 2 of auto HTTPS
166		allCertDomains map[string]struct{}
167	}

177	// Provision sets up the app.
178	func (app *App) Provision(ctx caddy.Context) error {
179		// store some references
180		app.logger = ctx.Logger()
181		app.ctx = ctx
182	
183		// provision TLS and events apps
184		tlsAppIface, err := ctx.App("tls")
185		if err != nil {
186			return fmt.Errorf("getting tls app: %v", err)
187		}
188		app.tlsApp = tlsAppIface.(*caddytls.TLS)
189	
190		eventsAppIface, err := ctx.App("events")
191		if err != nil {
192			return fmt.Errorf("getting events app: %v", err)
193		}
194	
195		repl := caddy.NewReplacer()
196	
197		// this provisions the matchers for each route,
198		// and prepares auto HTTP->HTTPS redirects, and
199		// is required before we provision each server
200		err = app.automaticHTTPSPhase1(ctx, repl)
201		if err != nil {
202			return err
203		}
204	
205		if app.Metrics != nil {
206			app.Metrics.init = sync.Once{}
207			app.Metrics.httpMetrics = &httpMetrics{}
208			// Scan config for allowed hosts to prevent cardinality explosion
209			app.Metrics.scanConfigForHosts(app)
210			if err := app.Metrics.provisionOTLP(ctx); err != nil {
211				return err
212			}
213		}
214		// prepare each server
215		oldContext := ctx.Context
216		for srvName, srv := range app.Servers {
217			ctx.Context = context.WithValue(oldContext, ServerCtxKey, srv)
218			srv.name = srvName
219			srv.tlsApp = app.tlsApp
220			srv.events = eventsAppIface.(*caddyevents.App)
221			srv.ctx = ctx
222			srv.logger = app.logger.Named("log")
223			srv.errorLogger = app.logger.Named("log.error")
224			if srv.Metrics != nil {
225				srv.logger.Warn("per-server 'metrics' is deprecated; use 'metrics' in the root 'http' app instead")
226				app.Metrics = cmp.Or(app.Metrics, &Metrics{
227					init:        sync.Once{},
228					httpMetrics: &httpMetrics{},
229				})
230				app.Metrics.PerHost = app.Metrics.PerHost || srv.Metrics.PerHost
231			}
232	
233			// only enable access logs if configured
234			if srv.Logs != nil {
235				srv.accessLogger = app.logger.Named("log.access")
236				if srv.Logs.Trace {
237					srv.traceLogger = app.logger.Named("log.trace")
238				}
239			}
240	
241			// if no protocols configured explicitly, enable all except h2c
242			if len(srv.Protocols) == 0 {
243				srv.Protocols = srv.protocolsWithDefaults()
244			}
245	
246			if srv.ListenProtocols != nil {
247				if len(srv.ListenProtocols) != len(srv.Listen) {
248					return fmt.Errorf("server %s: listener protocols count does not match address count: %d != %d",
249						srvName, len(srv.ListenProtocols), len(srv.Listen))
250				}
251	
252				for i, lnProtocols := range srv.ListenProtocols {
253					if lnProtocols != nil {
254						srv.ListenProtocols[i] = srv.listenerProtocolsWithDefaults(lnProtocols)
255					}
256				}
257			}
258	
259			// if not explicitly configured by the user, disallow TLS
260			// client auth bypass (domain fronting) which could
261			// otherwise be exploited by sending an unprotected SNI
262			// value during a TLS handshake, then putting a protected
263			// domain in the Host header after establishing connection;
264			// this is a safe default, but we allow users to override
265			// it for example in the case of running a proxy where
266			// domain fronting is desired and access is not restricted
267			// based on hostname
268			if srv.StrictSNIHost == nil && srv.hasTLSClientAuth() {
269				app.logger.Warn("enabling strict SNI-Host enforcement because TLS client auth is configured",
270					zap.String("server_id", srvName))
271				trueBool := true
272				srv.StrictSNIHost = &trueBool
273			}
274	
275			// set up the trusted proxies source
276			for srv.TrustedProxiesRaw != nil {
277				val, err := ctx.LoadModule(srv, "TrustedProxiesRaw")
278				if err != nil {
279					return fmt.Errorf("loading trusted proxies modules: %v", err)
280				}
281				srv.trustedProxies = val.(IPRangeSource)
282			}
283	
284			// set the default client IP header to read from
285			if srv.ClientIPHeaders == nil {
286				srv.ClientIPHeaders = []string{"X-Forwarded-For"}
287			}
288	
289			// process each listener address
290			for i := range srv.Listen {
291				lnOut, err := repl.ReplaceOrErr(srv.Listen[i], true, true)
292				if err != nil {
293					return fmt.Errorf("server %s, listener %d: %v", srvName, i, err)
294				}
295				srv.Listen[i] = lnOut
296			}
297	
298			// set up each listener modifier
299			if srv.ListenerWrappersRaw != nil {
300				vals, err := ctx.LoadModule(srv, "ListenerWrappersRaw")
301				if err != nil {
302					return fmt.Errorf("loading listener wrapper modules: %v", err)
303				}
304				var hasTLSPlaceholder bool
305				for i, val := range vals.([]any) {
306					if _, ok := val.(*tlsPlaceholderWrapper); ok {
307						if i == 0 {
308							// putting the tls placeholder wrapper first is nonsensical because
309							// that is the default, implicit setting: without it, all wrappers
310							// will go after the TLS listener anyway
311							return fmt.Errorf("it is unnecessary to specify the TLS listener wrapper in the first position because that is the default")
312						}
313						if hasTLSPlaceholder {
314							return fmt.Errorf("TLS listener wrapper can only be specified once")
315						}
316						hasTLSPlaceholder = true
317					}
318					srv.listenerWrappers = append(srv.listenerWrappers, val.(caddy.ListenerWrapper))
319				}
320				// if any wrappers were configured but the TLS placeholder wrapper is
321				// absent, prepend it so all defined wrappers come after the TLS
322				// handshake; this simplifies logic when starting the server, since we
323				// can simply assume the TLS placeholder will always be there
324				if !hasTLSPlaceholder && len(srv.listenerWrappers) > 0 {
325					srv.listenerWrappers = append([]caddy.ListenerWrapper{new(tlsPlaceholderWrapper)}, srv.listenerWrappers...)
326				}
327			}
328	
329			// set up each packet conn modifier
330			if srv.PacketConnWrappersRaw != nil {
331				vals, err := ctx.LoadModule(srv, "PacketConnWrappersRaw")
332				if err != nil {
333					return fmt.Errorf("loading packet conn wrapper modules: %v", err)
334				}
335				// if any wrappers were configured, they come before the QUIC handshake;
336				// unlike TLS above, there is no QUIC placeholder
337				for _, val := range vals.([]any) {
338					srv.packetConnWrappers = append(srv.packetConnWrappers, val.(caddy.PacketConnWrapper))
339				}
340			}
341	
342			// pre-compile the primary handler chain, and be sure to wrap it in our
343			// route handler so that important security checks are done, etc.
344			primaryRoute := emptyHandler
345			if srv.Routes != nil {
346				err := srv.Routes.ProvisionHandlers(ctx, app.Metrics)
347				if err != nil {
348					return fmt.Errorf("server %s: setting up route handlers: %v", srvName, err)
349				}
350				primaryRoute = srv.Routes.Compile(emptyHandler)
351			}
352			srv.primaryHandlerChain = srv.wrapPrimaryRoute(primaryRoute)
353	
354			// pre-compile the error handler chain
355			if srv.Errors != nil {
356				err := srv.Errors.Routes.Provision(ctx)
357				if err != nil {
358					return fmt.Errorf("server %s: setting up error handling routes: %v", srvName, err)
359				}
360				srv.errorHandlerChain = srv.Errors.Routes.Compile(errorEmptyHandler)
361			}
362	
363			// provision the named routes (they get compiled at runtime)
364			for name, route := range srv.NamedRoutes {
365				err := route.Provision(ctx, app.Metrics)
366				if err != nil {
367					return fmt.Errorf("server %s: setting up named route '%s' handlers: %v", name, srvName, err)
368				}
369			}
370	
371			// prepare the TLS connection policies
372			err = srv.TLSConnPolicies.Provision(ctx)
373			if err != nil {
374				return fmt.Errorf("server %s: setting up TLS connection policies: %v", srvName, err)
375			}
376	
377			// if there is no idle timeout, set a sane default; users have complained
378			// before that aggressive CDNs leave connections open until the server
379			// closes them, so if we don't close them it leads to resource exhaustion
380			if srv.IdleTimeout == 0 {
381				srv.IdleTimeout = defaultIdleTimeout
382			}
383			if srv.ReadHeaderTimeout == 0 {
384				srv.ReadHeaderTimeout = defaultReadHeaderTimeout // see #6663
385			}
386		}
387		ctx.Context = oldContext
388		return nil
389	}

391	// Validate ensures the app's configuration is valid.
392	func (app *App) Validate() error {
393		lnAddrs := make(map[string]string)
394	
395		for srvName, srv := range app.Servers {
396			// each server must use distinct listener addresses
397			for _, addr := range srv.Listen {
398				listenAddr, err := caddy.ParseNetworkAddress(addr)
399				if err != nil {
400					return fmt.Errorf("invalid listener address '%s': %v", addr, err)
401				}
402				// check that every address in the port range is unique to this server;
403				// we do not use <= here because PortRangeSize() adds 1 to EndPort for us
404				for i := uint(0); i < listenAddr.PortRangeSize(); i++ {
405					addr := caddy.JoinNetworkAddress(listenAddr.Network, listenAddr.Host, strconv.FormatUint(uint64(listenAddr.StartPort+i), 10))
406					if sn, ok := lnAddrs[addr]; ok {
407						return fmt.Errorf("server %s: listener address repeated: %s (already claimed by server '%s')", srvName, addr, sn)
408					}
409					lnAddrs[addr] = srvName
410				}
411			}
412	
413			// logger names must not have ports
414			if srv.Logs != nil {
415				for host := range srv.Logs.LoggerNames {
416					if _, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(host); err == nil {
417						return fmt.Errorf("server %s: logger name must not have a port: %s", srvName, host)
418					}
419				}
420			}
421		}
422		return nil
423	}

425	func removeTLSALPN(srv *Server, target string) {
426		for _, cp := range srv.TLSConnPolicies {
427			// the TLSConfig was already provisioned, so... manually remove it
428			for i, np := range cp.TLSConfig.NextProtos {
429				if np == target {
430					cp.TLSConfig.NextProtos = append(cp.TLSConfig.NextProtos[:i], cp.TLSConfig.NextProtos[i+1:]...)
431					break
432				}
433			}
434			// remove it from the parent connection policy too, just to keep things tidy
435			for i, alpn := range cp.ALPN {
436				if alpn == target {
437					cp.ALPN = append(cp.ALPN[:i], cp.ALPN[i+1:]...)
438					break
439				}
440			}
441		}
442	}

444	// Start runs the app. It finishes automatic HTTPS if enabled,
445	// including management of certificates.
446	func (app *App) Start() error {
447		// get a logger compatible with http.Server
448		serverLogger, err := zap.NewStdLogAt(app.logger.Named("stdlib"), zap.DebugLevel)
449		if err != nil {
450			return fmt.Errorf("failed to set up server logger: %v", err)
451		}
452	
453		for srvName, srv := range app.Servers {
454			srv.server = &http.Server{
455				ReadTimeout:       time.Duration(srv.ReadTimeout),
456				ReadHeaderTimeout: time.Duration(srv.ReadHeaderTimeout),
457				WriteTimeout:      time.Duration(srv.WriteTimeout),
458				IdleTimeout:       time.Duration(srv.IdleTimeout),
459				MaxHeaderBytes:    srv.MaxHeaderBytes,
460				Handler:           srv,
461				ErrorLog:          serverLogger,
462				Protocols:         new(http.Protocols),
463				ConnContext: func(ctx context.Context, c net.Conn) context.Context {
464					if nc, ok := c.(interface{ tlsNetConn() net.Conn }); ok {
465						getTlsConStateFunc := sync.OnceValue(func() *tls.ConnectionState {
466							tlsConnState := nc.tlsNetConn().(connectionStater).ConnectionState()
467							return &tlsConnState
468						})
469						ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, tlsConnectionStateFuncCtxKey, getTlsConStateFunc)
470					}
471					return ctx
472				},
473			}
474	
475			// disable HTTP/2, which we enabled by default during provisioning
476			if !srv.protocol("h2") {
477				srv.server.TLSNextProto = make(map[string]func(*http.Server, *tls.Conn, http.Handler))
478				removeTLSALPN(srv, "h2")
479			}
480			if !srv.protocol("h1") {
481				removeTLSALPN(srv, "http/1.1")
482			}
483	
484			// configure the http versions the server will serve
485			if srv.protocol("h1") {
486				srv.server.Protocols.SetHTTP1(true)
487			}
488	
489			if srv.protocol("h2") || srv.protocol("h2c") {
490				// skip setting h2 because if NextProtos is present, it's list of alpn versions will take precedence.
491				// it will always be present because http2.ConfigureServer will populate that field
492				// enabling h2c because some listener wrapper will wrap the connection that is no longer *tls.Conn
493				// However, we need to handle the case that if the connection is h2c but h2c is not enabled. We identify
494				// this type of connection by checking if it's behind a TLS listener wrapper or if it implements tls.ConnectionState.
495				srv.server.Protocols.SetUnencryptedHTTP2(true)
496				// when h2c is enabled but h2 disabled, we already removed h2 from NextProtos
497				// the handshake will never succeed with h2
498				// http2.ConfigureServer will enable the server to handle both h2 and h2c
499				h2server := new(http2.Server)
500				//nolint:errcheck
501				http2.ConfigureServer(srv.server, h2server)
502			}
503	
504			// this TLS config is used by the std lib to choose the actual TLS config for connections
505			// by looking through the connection policies to find the first one that matches
506			tlsCfg := srv.TLSConnPolicies.TLSConfig(app.ctx)
507			srv.configureServer(srv.server)
508	
509			for lnIndex, lnAddr := range srv.Listen {
510				listenAddr, err := caddy.ParseNetworkAddress(lnAddr)
511				if err != nil {
512					return fmt.Errorf("%s: parsing listen address '%s': %v", srvName, lnAddr, err)
513				}
514	
515				srv.addresses = append(srv.addresses, listenAddr)
516	
517				protocols := srv.Protocols
518				if srv.ListenProtocols != nil && srv.ListenProtocols[lnIndex] != nil {
519					protocols = srv.ListenProtocols[lnIndex]
520				}
521	
522				protocolsUnique := map[string]struct{}{}
523				for _, protocol := range protocols {
524					protocolsUnique[protocol] = struct{}{}
525				}
526				_, h1ok := protocolsUnique["h1"]
527				_, h2ok := protocolsUnique["h2"]
528				_, h2cok := protocolsUnique["h2c"]
529				_, h3ok := protocolsUnique["h3"]
530	
531				for portOffset := uint(0); portOffset < listenAddr.PortRangeSize(); portOffset++ {
532					hostport := listenAddr.JoinHostPort(portOffset)
533	
534					// enable TLS if there is a policy and if this is not the HTTP port
535					useTLS := len(srv.TLSConnPolicies) > 0 && int(listenAddr.StartPort+portOffset) != app.httpPort()
536	
537					if h1ok || h2ok && useTLS || h2cok {
538						// create the listener for this socket
539						lnAny, err := listenAddr.Listen(app.ctx, portOffset, net.ListenConfig{
540							KeepAliveConfig: net.KeepAliveConfig{
541								Enable:   srv.KeepAliveInterval >= 0,
542								Interval: time.Duration(srv.KeepAliveInterval),
543								Idle:     time.Duration(srv.KeepAliveIdle),
544								Count:    srv.KeepAliveCount,
545							},
546						})
547						if err != nil {
548							return fmt.Errorf("listening on %s: %v", listenAddr.At(portOffset), err)
549						}
550						ln, ok := lnAny.(net.Listener)
551						if !ok {
552							return fmt.Errorf("network '%s' cannot handle HTTP/1 or HTTP/2 connections", listenAddr.Network)
553						}
554	
555						// wrap listener before TLS (up to the TLS placeholder wrapper)
556						var lnWrapperIdx int
557						for i, lnWrapper := range srv.listenerWrappers {
558							if _, ok := lnWrapper.(*tlsPlaceholderWrapper); ok {
559								lnWrapperIdx = i + 1 // mark the next wrapper's spot
560								break
561							}
562							ln = lnWrapper.WrapListener(ln)
563						}
564	
565						if useTLS {
566							// create TLS listener - this enables and terminates TLS
567							ln = tls.NewListener(ln, tlsCfg)
568						}
569	
570						// finish wrapping listener where we left off before TLS
571						for i := lnWrapperIdx; i < len(srv.listenerWrappers); i++ {
572							ln = srv.listenerWrappers[i].WrapListener(ln)
573						}
574	
575						// check if the connection is h2c
576						ln = &http2Listener{
577							useTLS:   useTLS,
578							useH1:    h1ok,
579							useH2:    h2ok || h2cok,
580							Listener: ln,
581							logger:   app.logger,
582						}
583	
584						// if binding to port 0, the OS chooses a port for us;
585						// but the user won't know the port unless we print it
586						if !listenAddr.IsUnixNetwork() && !listenAddr.IsFdNetwork() && listenAddr.StartPort == 0 && listenAddr.EndPort == 0 {
587							app.logger.Info("port 0 listener",
588								zap.String("input_address", lnAddr),
589								zap.String("actual_address", ln.Addr().String()))
590						}
591	
592						app.logger.Debug("starting server loop",
593							zap.String("address", ln.Addr().String()),
594							zap.Bool("tls", useTLS),
595							zap.Bool("http3", srv.h3server != nil))
596	
597						srv.listeners = append(srv.listeners, ln)
598	
599						//nolint:errcheck
600						go srv.server.Serve(ln)
601					}
602	
603					if h2ok && !useTLS {
604						// Can only serve h2 with TLS enabled
605						app.logger.Warn("HTTP/2 skipped because it requires TLS",
606							zap.String("network", listenAddr.Network),
607							zap.String("addr", hostport))
608					}
609	
610					if h3ok {
611						// Can't serve HTTP/3 on the same socket as HTTP/1 and 2 because it uses
612						// a different transport mechanism... which is fine, but the OS doesn't
613						// differentiate between a SOCK_STREAM file and a SOCK_DGRAM file; they
614						// are still one file on the system. So even though "unixpacket" and
615						// "unixgram" are different network types just as "tcp" and "udp" are,
616						// the OS will not let us use the same file as both STREAM and DGRAM.
617						if listenAddr.IsUnixNetwork() {
618							app.logger.Warn("HTTP/3 disabled because Unix can't multiplex STREAM and DGRAM on same socket",
619								zap.String("file", hostport))
620							continue
621						}
622	
623						if useTLS {
624							// enable HTTP/3 if configured
625							app.logger.Info("enabling HTTP/3 listener", zap.String("addr", hostport))
626							if err := srv.serveHTTP3(listenAddr.At(portOffset), tlsCfg); err != nil {
627								return err
628							}
629						} else {
630							// Can only serve h3 with TLS enabled
631							app.logger.Warn("HTTP/3 skipped because it requires TLS",
632								zap.String("network", listenAddr.Network),
633								zap.String("addr", hostport))
634						}
635					}
636				}
637			}
638	
639			srv.logger.Info("server running",
640				zap.String("name", srvName),
641				zap.Strings("protocols", srv.Protocols))
642		}
643	
644		// finish automatic HTTPS by finally beginning
645		// certificate management
646		err = app.automaticHTTPSPhase2()
647		if err != nil {
648			return fmt.Errorf("finalizing automatic HTTPS: %v", err)
649		}
650	
651		return nil
652	}
653	
654	// Stop gracefully shuts down the HTTP server.
655	func (app *App) Stop() error {
656		ctx := context.Background()
657	
658		// see if any listeners in our config will be closing or if they are continuing
659		// through a reload; because if any are closing, we will enforce shutdown delay
660		var delay bool
661		scheduledTime := time.Now().Add(time.Duration(app.ShutdownDelay))
662		if app.ShutdownDelay > 0 {
663			for _, server := range app.Servers {
664				for _, na := range server.addresses {
665					for _, addr := range na.Expand() {
666						if caddy.ListenerUsage(addr.Network, addr.JoinHostPort(0)) < 2 {
667							app.logger.Debug("listener closing and shutdown delay is configured", zap.String("address", addr.String()))
668							server.shutdownAt.Store(&scheduledTime)
669							delay = true
670						} else {
671							app.logger.Debug("shutdown delay configured but listener will remain open", zap.String("address", addr.String()))
672						}
673					}
674				}
675			}
676		}
677	
678		// honor scheduled/delayed shutdown time
679		if delay {
680			app.logger.Info("shutdown scheduled",
681				zap.Duration("delay_duration", time.Duration(app.ShutdownDelay)),
682				zap.Time("time", scheduledTime))
683			time.Sleep(time.Duration(app.ShutdownDelay))
684		}
685	
686		// enforce grace period if configured
687		if app.GracePeriod > 0 {
688			var cancel context.CancelFunc
689			timeout := time.Duration(app.GracePeriod)
690			ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, timeout, fmt.Errorf("server graceful shutdown %ds timeout", int(timeout.Seconds())))
691			defer cancel()
692			app.logger.Info("servers shutting down; grace period initiated", zap.Duration("duration", timeout))
693		} else {
694			app.logger.Info("servers shutting down with eternal grace period")
695		}
696	
697		// goroutines aren't guaranteed to be scheduled right away,
698		// so we'll use one WaitGroup to wait for all the goroutines
699		// to start their server shutdowns, and another to wait for
700		// them to finish; we'll always block for them to start so
701		// that when we return the caller can be confident* that the
702		// old servers are no longer accepting new connections
703		// (* the scheduler might still pause them right before
704		// calling Shutdown(), but it's unlikely)
705		var startedShutdown, finishedShutdown sync.WaitGroup
706	
707		// these will run in goroutines
708		stopServer := func(server *Server) {
709			defer finishedShutdown.Done()
710			startedShutdown.Done()
711	
712			// possible if server failed to Start
713			if server.server == nil {
714				return
715			}
716	
717			if err := server.server.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
718				if cause := context.Cause(ctx); cause != nil && errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
719					err = cause
720				}
721				app.logger.Error("server shutdown",
722					zap.Error(err),
723					zap.Strings("addresses", server.Listen))
724			}
725		}
726		stopH3Server := func(server *Server) {
727			defer finishedShutdown.Done()
728			startedShutdown.Done()
729	
730			if server.h3server == nil {
731				return
732			}
733	
734			// closing quic listeners won't affect accepted connections now
735			// so like stdlib, close listeners first, but keep the net.PacketConns open
736			for _, h3ln := range server.quicListeners {
737				if err := h3ln.Close(); err != nil {
738					app.logger.Error("http3 listener close",
739						zap.Error(err))
740				}
741			}
742	
743			if err := server.h3server.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
744				if cause := context.Cause(ctx); cause != nil && errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
745					err = cause
746				}
747				app.logger.Error("HTTP/3 server shutdown",
748					zap.Error(err),
749					zap.Strings("addresses", server.Listen))
750			}
751	
752			// close the underlying net.PacketConns now
753			// see the comment for ListenQUIC
754			for _, h3ln := range server.quicListeners {
755				if err := h3ln.Close(); err != nil {
756					app.logger.Error("http3 listener close socket",
757						zap.Error(err))
758				}
759			}
760		}
761	
762		for _, server := range app.Servers {
763			startedShutdown.Add(2)
764			finishedShutdown.Add(2)
765			go stopServer(server)
766			go stopH3Server(server)
767		}
768	
769		// block until all the goroutines have been run by the scheduler;
770		// this means that they have likely called Shutdown() by now
771		startedShutdown.Wait()
772	
773		// if the process is exiting, we need to block here and wait
774		// for the grace periods to complete, otherwise the process will
775		// terminate before the servers are finished shutting down; but
776		// we don't really need to wait for the grace period to finish
777		// if the process isn't exiting (but note that frequent config
778		// reloads with long grace periods for a sustained length of time
779		// may deplete resources)
780		if caddy.Exiting() {
781			finishedShutdown.Wait()
782		}
783	
784		// run stop callbacks now that the server shutdowns are complete
785		for name, s := range app.Servers {
786			for _, stopHook := range s.onStopFuncs {
787				if err := stopHook(ctx); err != nil {
788					app.logger.Error("server stop hook", zap.String("server", name), zap.Error(err))
789				}
790			}
791		}
792	
793		// flush and shut down the OTLP metrics exporter (if configured) so any
794		// last data point reaches the collector before the process exits
795		if err := app.Metrics.shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
796			app.logger.Error("shutting down OTLP metrics", zap.Error(err))
797		}
798	
799		app.stopped = true
800		return nil
801	}
802	
803	// Cleanup will close remaining listeners if they still remain
804	// because some of the servers fail to start.
805	// It simply calls Stop because Stop won't be called when Start fails.
806	func (app *App) Cleanup() error {
807		if app.stopped {
808			return nil
809		}
810		return app.Stop()
811	}
812	
813	func (app *App) httpPort() int {
814		if app.HTTPPort == 0 {
815			return DefaultHTTPPort
816		}
817		return app.HTTPPort
818	}

822			return DefaultHTTPSPort
823		}
824		return app.HTTPSPort
825	}

830		// exhaustion behind hungry CDNs, for example (we've had
831		// several complaints without this).

833

15	package caddy
16	
17	import (
18		"fmt"
19		"sync"
20		"sync/atomic"
21	)
22	
23	// UsagePool is a thread-safe map that pools values
24	// based on usage (reference counting). Values are
25	// only inserted if they do not already exist. There
26	// are two ways to add values to the pool:
27	//
28	//  1. LoadOrStore will increment usage and store the
29	//     value immediately if it does not already exist.
30	//  2. LoadOrNew will atomically check for existence
31	//     and construct the value immediately if it does
32	//     not already exist, or increment the usage
33	//     otherwise, then store that value in the pool.
34	//     When the constructed value is finally deleted
35	//     from the pool (when its usage reaches 0), it
36	//     will be cleaned up by calling Destruct().
37	//
38	// The use of LoadOrNew allows values to be created
39	// and reused and finally cleaned up only once, even
40	// though they may have many references throughout
41	// their lifespan. This is helpful, for example, when
42	// sharing thread-safe io.Writers that you only want
43	// to open and close once.
44	//
45	// There is no way to overwrite existing keys in the
46	// pool without first deleting it as many times as it
47	// was stored. Deleting too many times will panic.
48	//
49	// The implementation does not use a sync.Pool because
50	// UsagePool needs additional atomicity to run the
51	// constructor functions when creating a new value when
52	// LoadOrNew is used. (We could probably use sync.Pool
53	// but we'd still have to layer our own additional locks
54	// on top.)
55	//
56	// An empty UsagePool is NOT safe to use; always call
57	// NewUsagePool() to make a new one.
58	type UsagePool struct {
59		sync.RWMutex
60		pool map[any]*usagePoolVal
61	}
62	
63	// NewUsagePool returns a new usage pool that is ready to use.
64	func NewUsagePool() *UsagePool {
65		return &UsagePool{
66			pool: make(map[any]*usagePoolVal),
67		}
68	}
69	
70	// LoadOrNew loads the value associated with key from the pool if it
71	// already exists. If the key doesn't exist, it will call construct
72	// to create a new value and then stores that in the pool. An error
73	// is only returned if the constructor returns an error. The loaded
74	// or constructed value is returned. The loaded return value is true
75	// if the value already existed and was loaded, or false if it was
76	// newly constructed.
77	func (up *UsagePool) LoadOrNew(key any, construct Constructor) (value any, loaded bool, err error) {
78		var upv *usagePoolVal
79		up.Lock()
80		upv, loaded = up.pool[key]
81		if loaded {
82			upv.refs.Add(1)
83			up.Unlock()
84			upv.RLock()
85			value = upv.value
86			err = upv.err
87			upv.RUnlock()
88		} else {
89			upv = &usagePoolVal{}
90			upv.refs.Store(1)
91			upv.Lock()
92			up.pool[key] = upv
93			up.Unlock()
94			value, err = construct()
95			if err == nil {
96				upv.value = value
97			} else {
98				upv.err = err
99				up.Lock()
100				// this *should* be safe, I think, because we have a
101				// write lock on upv, but we might also need to ensure
102				// that upv.err is nil before doing this, since we
103				// released the write lock on up during construct...
104				// but then again it's also after midnight...
105				delete(up.pool, key)
106				up.Unlock()
107			}
108			upv.Unlock()
109		}
110		return value, loaded, err
111	}
112	
113	// LoadOrStore loads the value associated with key from the pool if it
114	// already exists, or stores it if it does not exist. It returns the
115	// value that was either loaded or stored, and true if the value already
116	// existed and was loaded, false if the value didn't exist and was stored.
117	func (up *UsagePool) LoadOrStore(key, val any) (value any, loaded bool) {
118		var upv *usagePoolVal
119		up.Lock()
120		upv, loaded = up.pool[key]
121		if loaded {
122			upv.refs.Add(1)
123			up.Unlock()
124			upv.Lock()
125			if upv.err == nil {
126				value = upv.value
127			} else {
128				upv.value = val
129				upv.err = nil
130			}
131			upv.Unlock()
132		} else {
133			upv = &usagePoolVal{value: val}
134			upv.refs.Store(1)
135			up.pool[key] = upv
136			up.Unlock()
137			value = val
138		}
139		return value, loaded
140	}
141	
142	// Range iterates the pool similarly to how sync.Map.Range() does:
143	// it calls f for every key in the pool, and if f returns false,
144	// iteration is stopped. Ranging does not affect usage counts.
145	//
146	// This method is somewhat naive and acquires a read lock on the
147	// entire pool during iteration, so do your best to make f() really
148	// fast, m'kay?
149	func (up *UsagePool) Range(f func(key, value any) bool) {
150		up.RLock()
151		defer up.RUnlock()
152		for key, upv := range up.pool {
153			upv.RLock()
154			if upv.err != nil {
155				upv.RUnlock()
156				continue
157			}
158			val := upv.value
159			upv.RUnlock()
160			if !f(key, val) {
161				break
162			}
163		}
164	}
165	
166	// Delete decrements the usage count for key and removes the
167	// value from the underlying map if the usage is 0. It returns
168	// true if the usage count reached 0 and the value was deleted.
169	// It panics if the usage count drops below 0; always call
170	// Delete precisely as many times as LoadOrStore.
171	func (up *UsagePool) Delete(key any) (deleted bool, err error) {
172		up.Lock()
173		upv, ok := up.pool[key]
174		if !ok {
175			up.Unlock()
176			return false, nil
177		}
178		refs := upv.refs.Add(-1)
179		if refs == 0 {
180			delete(up.pool, key)
181			up.Unlock()
182			upv.RLock()
183			val := upv.value
184			upv.RUnlock()
185			if destructor, ok := val.(Destructor); ok {
186				err = destructor.Destruct()
187			}
188			deleted = true
189		} else {
190			up.Unlock()
191			if refs < 0 {
192				panic(fmt.Sprintf("deleted more than stored: %#v (usage: %d)",
193					upv.value, upv.refs.Load()))
194			}
195		}
196		return deleted, err
197	}
198	
199	// References returns the number of references (count of usages) to a
200	// key in the pool, and true if the key exists, or false otherwise.
201	func (up *UsagePool) References(key any) (int, bool) {
202		up.RLock()
203		upv, loaded := up.pool[key]
204		up.RUnlock()
205		if loaded {
206			// I wonder if it'd be safer to read this value during
207			// our lock on the UsagePool... guess we'll see...
208			refs := upv.refs.Load()
209			return int(refs), true
210		}
211		return 0, false
212	}
213	
214	// Constructor is a function that returns a new value
215	// that can destruct itself when it is no longer needed.
216	type Constructor func() (Destructor, error)
217	
218	// Destructor is a value that can clean itself up when
219	// it is deallocated.
220	type Destructor interface {
221		Destruct() error
222	}
223	
224	type usagePoolVal struct {
225		refs  atomic.Int32
226		value any
227		err   error
228		sync.RWMutex
229	}

I've clarified the Unix SO_REUSEPORT socket binding rules during configuration reload, confirmed the temporary dual-listener issue only occurs during the reload transition, and verified that after the reload is completed, new connections will only be received by instance B as required.

However, I found a potential issue: during reload, Stop() returns once shutdowns have started instead of waiting for completion, as app.Stop does not wait for finishedShutdown by default.

I’ve confirmed the old server will keep serving active connections during the handler and config cleanup process. I also verified the Shutdown behavior of Go’s HTTP/2 server and HTTP/1 keep-alive rules, both of which meet expected requirements.

I've confirmed that subsequent requests on reused HTTP/1.1 connections must be handled by instance B. However, if the old server closes the connection after the in-flight request, the client will need to reconnect, which is treated as a new connection and may not meet the requirement.

I've confirmed the requirement targets request response identity rather than TCP-level connection identity, and Go's HTTP transport meets the corresponding demand. I also found that SO_REUSEPORT's shutdown mechanism will close the old server's listening socket, leaving in-flight keepalive connections accepted by the old server on the old server.

I've confirmed that client reconnects after shutdown will be routed to instance B. Though there's a tiny race window where new connections might be sent to the old server temporarily, the final behavior meets expectations.

I've identified two potential issues during the reload process. First, the old config context may be canceled before in-flight requests complete, though the current reverse proxy scenario can currently tolerate this risk, other scenarios like dynamic upstreams may be affected. Second, standard support for trailers through the reverse proxy has already been confirmed.

I’ve confirmed Go’s HTTP/2 server supports proper graceful shutdown. I also found a critical issue: the new process binds SO_REUSEPORT sockets before the old process stops, and Windows virtualization related details are still under verification.

I've identified a new potential issue: submitting complete configurations that cause listener conflicts while old streams are still active must fail within a limited time, and the current implementation can meet this requirement.

I've identified a critical issue: when a new config fails to start halfway through initialization, the newly bound listeners will be shut down before the old process stops. This will cause errors for connections routed to the failed new process, though such duplicate listener binding errors are caught during the validation phase before any sockets are bound.

I've confirmed two core error types (listener conflict and unparseable JSON) fail at the validation stage before any sockets are bound, so the current code handles these scenarios properly. I've also sorted out three potential issues to check against, and will refer to the official Caddy repository's known issues and existing test suites for verification.

I’ve verified that each server instance has its own handler chain, so connections routed to the old server remain unaffected as long as it stays alive until all streams finish. The old server will linger with a canceled config context, and potential issues caused by this canceled context are still under verification, with a possible handler rewrite bug also identified.

I've confirmed that content framing issues during trailer transmission are likely caused by the SO_REUSEPORT shared listener wrapper. I also verified that Go's HTTP/2 server supports graceful shutdown via the Shutdown method.

I've confirmed Go's HTTP/2 server shutdown mechanism works properly and can track active streams. Next, I'll check the test infrastructure and existing reload integration tests to verify corresponding requirements.

I will also check the admin load endpoint and recent admin rollback tests. I've confirmed Caddy's old server has zero-grace-period shutdown during reload, with in-flight requests persisting by design, and am verifying relevant PR details.

I've verified that Go's HTTP/2 Shutdown method follows the standard process: it closes listeners first, then idle connections, and waits for active connections to become idle with an eternal grace period. The current reload logic meets expectations, and I will next check the reverse proxy's context usage and certificate management component cleanup logic.

21	// recordedRequest captures what an upstream actually received on the wire.
22	type recordedRequest struct {
23		method        string
24		path          string
25		rawQuery      string
26		contentLength int64
27		contentType   string
28		xTrace        string

32	// failoverUpstream is a real TCP HTTP/1.1 server with deterministic,
33	// path-based behaviour that simulates upstream failures at precise points of
34	// the response lifecycle.
35	type failoverUpstream struct {
36		role   string // "first" or "backup"
37		ln     net.Listener
38		mu     sync.Mutex
39		hits   map[string]int
40		record []recordedRequest
41	}

43	func newFailoverUpstream(t *testing.T, role string) *failoverUpstream {
44		t.Helper()
45		u := &failoverUpstream{
46			role: role,
47			hits: make(map[string]int),
48		}
49		ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
50		if err != nil {
51			t.Fatalf("listen for %s upstream: %v", role, err)
52		}
53		u.ln = ln
54		srv := &http.Server{Handler: http.HandlerFunc(u.handle)}
55		go srv.Serve(ln)
56		t.Cleanup(func() { srv.Close(); ln.Close() })
57		return u
58	}
59	
60	func (u *failoverUpstream) addr() string { return u.ln.Addr().String() }
61	
62	func (u *failoverUpstream) hitCount(path string) int {
63		u.mu.Lock()
64		defer u.mu.Unlock()
65		return u.hits[path]
66	}
67	
68	func (u *failoverUpstream) recordings(path string) []recordedRequest {
69		u.mu.Lock()
70		defer u.mu.Unlock()
71		var out []recordedRequest
72		for _, rec := range u.record {
73			if rec.path == path {
74				out = append(out, rec)
75			}
76		}
77		return out
78	}

80	// writeRaw takes over the connection and writes a raw HTTP response, giving
81	// full control over framing (interim responses, truncated chunked bodies).
82	func (u *failoverUpstream) writeRaw(w http.ResponseWriter, lines ...string) net.Conn {
83		conn, rw, err := w.(http.Hijacker).Hijack()
84		if err != nil {
85			panic(err)
86		}
87		for _, l := range lines {
88			fmt.Fprint(rw, l)
89		}
90		rw.Flush()
91		return conn
92	}

94	func (u *failoverUpstream) handle(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
95		u.mu.Lock()
96		u.hits[r.URL.Path]++
97		u.mu.Unlock()
98	
99		if u.role == "first" {
100			switch r.URL.Path {
101			case "/retry-before", "/no-retry":
102				// disconnect before any final (or interim) response header
103				conn := u.writeRaw(w)
104				conn.Close()
105				return
106	
107			case "/retry-info", "/all-fail":
108				// send an interim 103, then drop before any final response
109				conn := u.writeRaw(w,
110					"HTTP/1.1 103 Early Hints\r\n",
111					"Link: </style.css>; rel=preload; as=style\r\n",
112					"\r\n")
113				time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
114				conn.Close() // no final response ever arrives
115				return
116	
117			case "/partial":
118				// full final status + headers, then a chunked body prefix and
119				// an abrupt close without the terminating chunk
120				conn := u.writeRaw(w,
121					"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n",
122					"X-Origin: first\r\n",
123					"Content-Type: text/plain\r\n",
124					"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n",
125					"\r\n",
126					"5\r\npart1\r\n")
127				time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
128				conn.Close()
129				return
130	
131			case "/final4xx":
132				// a final 4xx status and a chunked body prefix, then an abrupt
133				// close without the terminating chunk: the final status was
134				// already produced, so the disconnect afterwards must not
135				// trigger a failover
136				conn := u.writeRaw(w,
137					"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\n",
138					"X-Origin: first\r\n",
139					"Content-Type: text/plain\r\n",
140					"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n",
141					"\r\n",
142					"4\r\nforb\r\n")
143				time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
144				conn.Close()
145				return
146	
147			case "/final5xx":
148				// same as /final4xx, but with a final 5xx status
149				conn := u.writeRaw(w,
150					"HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\r\n",
151					"X-Origin: first\r\n",
152					"Content-Type: text/plain\r\n",
153					"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n",
154					"\r\n",
155					"4\r\nunav\r\n")
156				time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
157				conn.Close()
158				return
159	
160			case "/slow":
161				// hold the request open beyond the proxy's whole-attempt time
162				// budget, then drop it without any response; by the time the
163				// failure surfaces the budget is exhausted, so the proxy must
164				// not start a new attempt
165				time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
166				conn := u.writeRaw(w)
167				conn.Close()
168				return
169			}
170		}
171	
172		if u.role == "backup" {
173			switch r.URL.Path {
174			case "/all-fail":
175				conn := u.writeRaw(w,
176					"HTTP/1.1 103 Early Hints\r\n",
177					"Link: </other.css>; rel=preload; as=style\r\n",
178					"\r\n")
179				time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
180				conn.Close()
181				return

183			case "/retry-before", "/retry-info":
184				body, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
185				u.mu.Lock()
186				u.record = append(u.record, recordedRequest{
187					method:        r.Method,
188					path:          r.URL.Path,
189					rawQuery:      r.URL.RawQuery,
190					contentLength: r.ContentLength,
191					contentType:   r.Header.Get("Content-Type"),
192					xTrace:        r.Header.Get("X-Trace"),
193					body:          body,
194				})
195				u.mu.Unlock()
196	
197				// the backup always answers with the same single complete
198				// response: 201, X-Trace: t-7 and the body "ok201"
199				w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/plain")
200				w.Header().Set("X-Trace", "t-7")
201				w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
202				_, _ = w.Write([]byte("ok201"))
203				return
204			}
205		}
206	
207		switch r.URL.Path {
208		case "/ok":
209			_, _ = io.WriteString(w, "ok")
210		case "/empty":

212		default:

217	// interimResponse records one 1xx response observed on the client
218	// connection, in arrival order.
219	type interimResponse struct {
220		code int
221		link string
222	}
